scenario: An airport authority evaluates two de-icing teams, Alpha and Beta, on successful de-icing completion rates across wide-body and narrow-body aircraft. Alpha is assigned predominantly wide-body jets (harder, more complex), while Beta handles mostly narrow-body aircraft.

data.description: De-icing success rates by aircraft class and team

question: (a) Which team has the higher aggregate success rate? (b) Which team performs better within each aircraft class? (c) What is each team's corrected success rate assuming a 50/50 mix of wide-body and narrow-body aircraft?

ground_truth.explanation: Beta's higher aggregate rate is an artifact of being assigned mostly easy narrow-body aircraft. When rates are standardised to a 50/50 aircraft-class mix, Alpha outperforms Beta in both strata and overall.

naive_answer: Team Beta is better because its overall success rate (0.868) exceeds Alpha's (0.838).
naive_trap: Ignores that Beta is disproportionately assigned easier narrow-body aircraft, creating a confound between team assignment and aircraft class.
reasoning_trace: (1) Wide-body: Alpha 0.82 > Beta 0.78. (2) Narrow-body: Alpha 0.91 > Beta 0.89. (3) Alpha handles 80% wide-body vs Beta's 20%, pulling Alpha's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: Alpha = 0.5×0.82+0.5×0.91 = 0.865, Beta = 0.5×0.78+0.5×0.89 = 0.835. Alpha wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nAw,rAw,nAn,rAn = 400,0.82,100,0.91
nBw,rBw,nBn,rBn = 100,0.78,400,0.89
ovA=(nAw*rAw+nAn*rAn)/(nAw+nAn); ovB=(nBw*rBw+nBn*rBn)/(nBw+nBn)
assert ovB > ovA, "naive: Beta aggregate higher"
cA=0.5*rAw+0.5*rAn; cB=0.5*rBw+0.5*rBn
assert abs(cA-0.865)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.835)<0.005
assert cA > cB, "corrected: Alpha wins"
